questions.key_step: Allied angles reduce every term to $\pm\tan15^\circ$, then $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\frac{2}{\sin2\theta}$.
questions.justification: Standard allied-angle reduction plus one identity; single familiar trick.
One recognised identity applied four times plus reduction of $729^\circ$; a few chained routine steps.
Textbook sine-doubling product; one well-known trick applied once.

questions.key_step: Pair $\tan x$ with $\cot x$ to get $\frac{2}{\sin2x}$, then exact values of $\sin18^\circ,\sin54^\circ$.
questions.justification: Several routine steps (tan+cot pairing, exact values of $\sin18^\circ$, rationalising) with a numerical answer and no options.

questions.key_step: Complementary angles give $\tan\theta_1\tan\theta_2=1$; with the tangent sum this fixes the angles; area fixes scale.
questions.justification: Figure setup, tangent sum/product, choosing the larger-ratio root, then area to scale: chain of routine steps.

questions.key_step: Addition formula; $\tan A\tan B=\frac{1}{x^2+x+1}$ simplifies $1-\tan A\tan B$.
questions.justification: Addition formula with surd algebra, simplifying a messy fraction; routine but multi-step. Options allow a test value.

questions.key_step: Read $\tan x$ and $\cos x$ off the 3-4-5 triangle with quadrant signs.
questions.justification: Direct evaluation from a 3-4-5 triangle; no decision except quadrant sign.
